source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Keep all PPE on until reaching the nurses' station so every item can be removed at one location","B":"Remove the respirator inside the patient room before removing contaminated gloves and gown","C":"Remove other PPE before leaving the care area, then remove the respirator after exit and door closure","D":"Remove PPE in any order or location because correct hand hygiene makes doffing sequence irrelevant"}}
source_row.rationale: CDC core practices direct healthcare personnel to remove and discard PPE other than respirators before leaving the patient room or care area. A respirator is removed after leaving the room or care area and closing the door, with hand hygiene performed appropriately.
source_row.source_detail: CDC Core Infection Prevention Practices: remove non-respirator PPE before leaving care area; respirator after exit/door closure; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: CDC — PPE Doffing Sequence for Airborne Infection Isolation Rooms
source_row.stem: A nurse is leaving an airborne-precaution room after completing care. Which PPE-removal principle is correct?
